model_output.summary: Leading mechanical design for the Arlo height-adjustable desk places you at the center of a named product platform. Your progression at Westhaven and current Engineer II title point to an individual contributor role with design leadership. The work spans drawings, analysis, suppliers, and manufacturing support. What remains unclear is which design choices or product problems were yours to resolve, making the breadth easier to see than your contribution to a finished product.
strengths: Supplier work in Mexico and Taiwan shows that your role extends beyond internal design tasks.
BIFMA prototype testing ties your earlier engineering work to a named furniture standard.
SolidWorks, GD&T, and load-bearing component analysis give a reviewer concrete technical context.
gaps: The Arlo bullet does not identify the parts or design decisions you led, leaving the extent of your platform responsibility unclear.
The first-article inspection bullet does not say what you reviewed or resolved with suppliers, making your part in that process difficult to assess.
No project result or completed product change is described, so the reader cannot connect your work to what ultimately shipped or changed.
